rationale:
`assets/skills/habeas/SKILL.md` is a bundled skill with front matter, so it is a site of `requirements.cli.skill_conventions.references`. The requirement obliges each link to a specialized file to say when to read it. The file has three such links, and each one says when:

- `[CI example](references/ci.md)` comes after "Use the ... when adding these steps to an existing workflow", and the sentence before it covers "setting up or reviewing project CI".
- `[references/distributed-requirements.md]` is introduced with "read ... before drafting it, and whenever you edit a `{req}` that contains `{sites}` or `{violations}`". The text before it gives the situation: an obligation that applies separately at each of many sites.
- `[references/syntax-details.md]` is introduced with "If a file that implements or tests a requirement cannot carry a comment, such as a shipped skill or a stylesheet..., or a requirement lives in a nested chapter, read ...".

The mention of `references/fixme.md` is inline code naming another skill's file, not a link. It also says when to use it, since the gap is deferred and `{fixme}` acknowledges it. No violation queries are listed for this requirement. I found no link without a reading condition.

text: A bundled skill MAY put material needed only in specialized situations in files it links to. Each such link MUST say when to read the file. Each bundled skill, recognized by its front matter, is a site:
